identification.summary: Moshen Dragon is a China-aligned cyberespionage cluster named by SentinelLabs in May 2022 that targeted telecommunication providers in Central Asia [S1][S2][S4]. It sideloaded ShadowPad and PlugX through DLL search order hijacking of legitimate security-vendor software [S1][S2].
identification.firstObserved: May 2022 (date of SentinelLabs public reporting, as relayed by secondary coverage); earlier activity start date not confirmed in sources gathered [S1][S2].
identification.notes: No Microsoft name is recorded for this cluster. Secondary reporting says researchers saw tactical overlap with Nomad Panda (RedFoxtrot) but SentinelLabs tracks the groups separately [S1].

attribution.confidence: SentinelLabs describes the cluster as China-aligned [S1][S4]. No government attribution found in sources gathered.
attribution.basis: Malware choice (ShadowPad, PlugX) and TTP overlap with other China-linked groups, as reported by SentinelLabs via secondary coverage [S1].

objectives: Espionage against the telecommunications sector in Central Asia, as characterized by SentinelLabs [S1][S4]. Specific collection requirements are not stated in the sources gathered.

targeting.notes: Specific victim organizations and countries are not named in the secondary sources gathered [S1][S2].

capabilities.summary: Five malware 'triads' (loader, DLL, payload sets) that use DLL search order hijacking against signed security software from Symantec, Trend Micro, BitDefender, McAfee and Kaspersky to sideload ShadowPad and PlugX [S1][S2]. Additional tools reported are an LSA notification package for credential harvesting, the passive backdoor GUNTERS, and Impacket for lateral movement and exfiltration [S1][S4]. SentinelLabs said it could not determine the initial infection vector [S2]. The abuse relies on a Windows design weakness, not vulnerabilities in the security products [S2].

campaigns.name: SentinelLabs disclosure of telecom targeting in Central Asia
campaigns.summary: SentinelLabs published 'Moshen Dragon's Triad-and-Error Approach', reporting ShadowPad and PlugX sideloading against Central Asian telecom operators [S1][S2].

diamond.adversary: China-aligned espionage cluster tracked as Moshen Dragon by SentinelLabs [S1][S4].
diamond.capability: ShadowPad and PlugX delivered via DLL search order hijacking of security-vendor binaries; LSA notification package; GUNTERS passive backdoor; Impacket [S1][S2][S4].
diamond.technology: Windows hosts running security software whose signed binaries load DLLs from writable search paths [S2].

gaps: Could not open the primary SentinelLabs report or other pages (DNS failure in this environment); all facts rely on search-result summaries of secondary coverage and must be verified against the original.
Initial access vector was not determined by SentinelLabs [S2].
Victim names, countries, timeline and dwell time are not identified in the sources gathered.
No sponsor or government attribution found. Overlap with RedFoxtrot/Nomad Panda (reported by Recorded Future as likely tied to PLA Unit 69010) is TTP-level only; do not merge clusters [S1].
No Microsoft name, MITRE group ID or post-2022 activity was found.
Infrastructure indicators (domains, IPs, hashes) not collected.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Telecommunications providers and the endpoints and servers running security software are relevant terrain for coalition and partner-nation communications in Central Asia [S1][S4]. STEP 2: Security-vendor binaries are trusted by defenders, so sideloading hides in plain sight [S2]. STEP 3: The pattern is unknown access, then DLL-sideloaded ShadowPad/PlugX, credential theft via an LSA notification package, lateral movement with Impacket [S1][S4]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued telecom-sector espionage in Central Asia. MDCOA (low-evidence extrapolation) is use of telecom access to support collection against partner governments. Candidate indicators: legitimate AV executables running from unusual directories, unsigned DLLs beside signed binaries, new LSA notification packages, Impacket-style lateral movement [S1][S2][S4].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track partner-nation telecom compromise reporting for Central Asia [S1]. (2) Authorities: hunting on partner or commercial telecom networks requires host-nation or provider consent. (3) Mission assurance: do not assume signed security-vendor binaries are benign; add DLL load-path monitoring [S2]. (4) Coordination: share indicators through established vendor and partner channels; initial access is unknown, so avoid over-specific guidance [S2].
